C-RELEASE-BETA-CHECKS-GATE.Summary: Give the release workflow's prerelease lane a lightweight required-checks gate: a beta/canary tag may build and publish only when the pinned required checks on its exact tag commit are present and green, without reintroducing the heavy stable-lane gates.
C-RELEASE-BETA-CHECKS-GATE.Problem: The prerelease lane (C-RELEASE-CANARY-PRERELEASE, release.yml v3.7.0) skips every checks-verification step: authorize-tag gates "read exact payload check runs" (~184), "strict online release admission" (~195), "materials and version admission" (~204) and the release-identity artifact upload (~212) behind `prerelease != 'true'`, and build repeats the skip for the admitted-evidence download and repeated strict admission (~410-441). A beta/canary tag therefore reaches external testers as a signed, notarized GitHub prerelease with zero evidence that its commit's CI was green — a red-CI commit can ship. Audit finding ci/cd 49 (21-section digest, 2026-11-21). The stable lane proves the pattern: it collects check runs for the payload SHA into a digest-verified checks file and requires the strict set green; the beta lane verifies nothing about its commit's CI state.

Goals.Goal: The prerelease lane of authorize-tag collects check runs for the tag's HEAD SHA (the seal) using the same collection shape as the stable lane (paginated check-runs API, deduplicated per name+app keeping the latest attempt, one checks file), then a new lightweight gate step requires every pinned prerelease required check to exist exactly once at that SHA with conclusion success; a failed, cancelled, or missing check — or a check recorded at any other SHA — fails authorize-tag before the release-signing environment or any packaging job runs.

The prerelease required-checks set is pinned explicitly in release.yml as the two main-branch required contexts derivable from .github/release-governance.json (rulesets.main.requiredChecks minus the tag-time-only release/readiness): "status check" (GitHub Actions) — test.yml's aggregate over the renderer-unit and backend-unit matrices, e2e and quicklook-native, i.e. the core build matrix + test lanes — and "release/governance" (GitHub Actions). Both workflows run on every push to main, so every main commit a beta tag can name carries both check runs at its exact SHA.

Re-runs are idempotent: the gate consumes check runs freshly collected from the API on every run attempt, with no artifact, cache, or cross-run state on the prerelease path, so a re-run after a flaky red or an incomplete first attempt re-evaluates current data instead of wedging the lane.

Source-pinned structural tests in the established governance-test pattern pin the new gate: the explicit prerelease required-checks list, the prerelease-only step condition, and the fail-closed evaluation against deterministic red fixtures (failure, cancelled, missing, wrong SHA, superseded rerun), plus a red control rejecting a workflow where the gate or the pinned list is absent.

docs/release-process.md section 4a (Prerelease builds for external testers) states that a prerelease tag run verifies its commit's required checks and that the gate fails closed until main CI is green at the tagged commit.

Constraints.Constraint: ObservedWriteScope: .github/workflows/release.yml; its source pins in tests/renderer/release-governance.test.js; .grace/graph/features.xml (M-046 SummaryDelta); .grace/verification/features.xml (V-M-046 commands); docs/release-process.md section 4a only because the manual protocol already documents the beta path; release.yml's own GRACE markup (MODULE_CONTRACT/MODULE_MAP/CHANGE_SUMMARY with a version bump). No Rust, no renderer product code, no new workflow files, tools, secrets, environments, or npm dependencies.

The prerelease lane stays lightweight and owner-gated exactly as designed by C-RELEASE-CANARY-PRERELEASE: no Ready seal, no strict admission, no materials, no metadata preflight, no release-identity artifact, no payload-seal evidence, and the unchanged synchronous release environment approval on publish. Only the checks verification is added.

The stable path stays byte-identical for non-hyphenated tags: every step condition, the strict admission set, the digest-verified release-identity artifact, feed-advance verification and the cask handoff keep their current behavior; the shared collection step, if unified, must produce the identical checks-file format for both lanes (strictness differs only in which set is required).

The gate lives in authorize-tag (which already holds checks: read) and fails closed; publish is protected transitively because build requires authorize-tag success and publish requires build. No new job, no branch-protection or ruleset API calls, no change to .github/release-governance.json, no new required-check configuration surface outside the workflow source.
The edit is actionlint-clean; no new permissions beyond the job's existing contents: read and checks: read; the gate step must not swallow the evaluation's exit status.

GRACE bookkeeping is synchronized: release.yml MODULE_MAP gains the gate description in authorize-tag, CHANGE_SUMMARY gains the C-RELEASE-BETA-CHECKS-GATE entry with a version bump, and the graph and verification files describe the added prerelease boundary.

NonGoals.NonGoal: Any change to stable-lane behavior: the strict admission set, materials gate, preflight, identity artifact, feed-advance assertion and cask handoff remain untouched for non-hyphenated tags.
No new jobs for materials, payload-seal evidence, readiness-strict, or reviewed release materials on the prerelease lane; the beta gate is checks-only.

No branch-protection or ruleset API calls, no live ruleset enforcement changes, and no extension of the governance config; the prerelease required set is pinned in the workflow source, deliberately redundant to the config, so the gate cannot silently drift with a config edit.
No canary updater feed, in-app channel switcher, or changes to release/promote dispatch, publish ordering, or the updater client.

No closing of the residual TOCTOU window between the authorize-tag check and publication (a re-run of a required check turning red after the gate); closing it with a build-side re-verification would reintroduce weight the finding explicitly excludes and is a separate scope decision.

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: release.yml contains an explicit prerelease required-checks list pinning exactly {name: "status check", app: "GitHub Actions"} and {name: "release/governance", app: "GitHub Actions"} with a comment recording why release/readiness is excluded (tag-time check of this very workflow, cannot pre-exist on the beta commit) and citing .github/release-governance.json rulesets.main.requiredChecks as the derivation source.

authorize-tag has a prerelease-only collection step (conditioned on the identity step's prerelease output equal to 'true') writing the checks file in the stable lane's exact JSON shape, and a prerelease-only gate step that fails on: conclusion failure, conclusion cancelled, a required name missing from the collection, a match recorded at a SHA other than the tag's HEAD SHA, or more than one live match per required identity. Non-hyphenated tags keep the existing steps and conditions unchanged.

Deterministic fixtures prove fail-closed evaluation: fixture JSON with a "status check" conclusion failure fails; with it cancelled fails; with it absent fails; with success but at a stale SHA fails; with all required checks success at the exact seal SHA passes; and a fixture carrying a superseded earlier attempt plus a later success resolves to the latest attempt and passes (the existing sort-by-started-time, group-by-name-and-app, keep-last shape).

The structural test red control rejects a workflow source where the prerelease required-checks list or the prerelease-only gate step is removed, and rejects a gate step not conditioned to run only for prereleases; the existing stable-lane pins in tests/renderer/release-governance.test.js keep passing.

Re-run idempotency is pinned structurally: the prerelease gate path reads only from check runs collected within the same run attempt (no download-artifact, cache action, or persisted state on that path), so a rerun after a flaky red re-collects fresh evidence and recovers without manual intervention.

GRACE bookkeeping is synchronized and the focused verification is green: release.yml markup updated with a version bump, M-046 SummaryDelta present, V-M-046 commands updated, actionlint clean on release.yml, and the governance plus action-reference test files pass.

VerificationIntent.ExpectedEvidence: Green structural pins and red-fixture evidence for failure, cancelled, missing, stale-SHA and rerun-supersession cases; a workflow diff limited to the prerelease-lane steps, GRACE markup and docs section 4a; actionlint clean; after merge, the first real beta/canary tag run serves as live evidence — the gate step green in the authorize-tag log at the tag SHA, and one forced red control recorded as rejected by the gate.

Assumptions.Assumption: A beta tag names a commit on main, where test.yml and release-governance.yml both run on push and report check runs at the exact commit SHA; docs-only merges report the aggregate "status check" green via job-level skips, so the pinned set is satisfiable for every main commit shape.

The gate failing closed while main CI is still running at the tagged commit is intended behavior: release/promote should be invoked after the commit's main CI is green, or the release workflow re-run afterwards; idempotent re-collection makes such a re-run safe.

release/readiness stays excluded from the beta required set because it is produced by authorize-tag itself on the tag event; if the owner instead wants publication-time enforcement, moving the gate to the publish job is the documented alternative, not an addition to this change.
